newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil massacre trial of 17 policemen postponed.
newsitem.headline: Brazil massacre trial of 17 policemen postponed.

text.p: A Brazilian court on Wednesday postponed the trial of 17 police officers accused of gunning down 21 people in Rio de Janeiro's Vigario Geral shantytown in 1993.

Judge Jose Geraldo Antonio told the Rio de Janeiro state court that the first trial in the case would be adjourned due to new evidence. He said a new forensic report implicated police officers who were arrested initially and later freed.
The trial of 16 defendants has been postponed indefinitely and the prosecution and defence teams have 10 days to order further investigations on the basis of the forensic report.
Only one defendant in the case, Paulo Roberto Alvarenga, who claims to be innocent and wants to be judged as soon as possible, will appear in court on April 24.

A total of 52 police officers are accused of involvement in the killings on Aug. 30, 1993, when about 20 hooded gunmen dressed in black and armed with automatic weapons and shotguns opened fire on Vigario Geral's residents to avenge the death of four policemen.
The massacre took place hours after four military police officers died in an ambush by alleged drug traffickers.

The 52 police officers are being tried in two separate court processes. In the first one, which includes Wednesday's 17, a total of 33 policemen is being tried, while the second one deals with the remaining 19.

The new forensic report was drawn up after the bodies of 19 victims were exhumed in October last year to be re-checked for bullets. Relatives of victims had found bullets in the other two bodies which led authorities to review the original autopsies.

The accused face sentences of several hundred years in jail if found guilty on charges of murder and attempted murder. However, under Brazilian law no prisoner may serve more than 30 years, regardless of the sentence.
